summary: Split-tunnel routes not re-applied after suspend/resume on Windows 11 with Peplink client
description: Issue summary: After suspending and resuming a Windows 11 laptop (close lid / sleep / resume) the Peplink VPN client connects successfully but the split-tunnel route policy is not re-applied. Impact: Affected endpoints lose access to private subnets (internal APIs, vault, internal CI agents) until the user toggles the VPN adapter or reboots. This is reproducible on multiple MacBook Pro M-series (running Windows 11 via Bootcamp/Parallels) and corporate Lenovo ThinkPads. Scope: Reported by 6 users in engineering (us-west) over the last week; potential to block on-call access to internal tools during travel/meetings. Observed behaviour: VPN shows as connected in client, DNS resolves public domains correctly, internal routes (10.20.0.0/16, 10.21.0.0/16) missing from the routing table. Expected behaviour: On resume the client should re-assert the split-tunnel routes and enforce internal DNS for internal domains.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Login to Windows 11 device with Peplink VPN client v2.2.8 installed.
2) Establish VPN connection to Redwood Peplink edge (profile: corporate-split-tunnel).
3) Verify internal routes present (route print /nz).
4) Suspend system (close lid or select Sleep).
5) Resume system and allow client to reconnect automatically.
6) Check routing table and internal connectivity (curl http://internal-api.redwood.local).
Expected: internal routes present and API reachable. Actual: routes missing and API times out.

investigation_notes:
Hypotheses tested:
- H1: Windows 11 changed power/resume events such that RAS/VPN rebind events are not triggered consistently. Verified: Rebind callback not fired on two Lenovo devices.
- H2: Peplink client v2.2.8 has a race between service restart and route application after resume. Verified: adding a 3s forced retry to the RouteManager causes routes to appear.
- H3: Group Policy / local firewall blocking route addition after resume. Verified: GPO not changed and local firewall logs do not show blocked netsh calls.
Telemetry checked:
- Support traces from affected hosts live at s3://support-traces/INT-67120/ (redacted)
- Netsh output and RouteManager debug shows route-apply call succeeded but Windows kernel returned ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER in some runs.
Repro matrix:
- Windows 10 (older corp fleet): no issue observed.
- Windows 11 (22H2 and 23H2 variants): consistent failure on machines using Peplink client installed via SCCM/Intune.
- Third-party VPN clients (IKEv2 based) reapply routes correctly on resume.
Preliminary root cause: a timing/regression in Peplink client v2.2.8 where the VPN service declares CONNECTED before the OS networking stack is fully ready to accept route modifications after resume. Windows 11 resumed networking state appears to be delayed relative to the service event.
resolution:
Workaround (documented to affected teams): 1) Toggle the Peplink adapter: disable/enable network adapter via UI or run 'netsh interface set interface "PeplinkVPN" admin=disabled' then re-enable. 2) Run 'netsh interface ipv4 add route 10.20.0.0/16 "PeplinkVPN" 0' as temporary script.
Short-term fix: We have prepared a hotfix build v2.2.9 that adds a delayed route-apply retry loop (3 retries, 2s backoff) on resume and validates route presence before marking CONNECTED. QA validated on 10 Windows 11 devices.
Rollout plan: Canary push to 10 internal users on 2026-03-15, wider auto-upgrade to corp fleet on 2026-03-18 pending canary metrics.
Follow-up actions:
- Track any further reports in SUP slack channel #support.
- Add a Confluence entry with the suspend/resume troubleshooting checklist and include netsh remediation steps.
- Create a follow-up engineering ticket to harden route application across other vendors (INT-67145).
